title: Capstone lab: diagnose a broken release bundle and hand it off
markdown:
## Why this matters

The capstone asks for what the course has been building toward: a diagnosis someone else can verify. A simulated release bundle has three problems hidden in ordinary places: a path that does not match the filesystem, a permission that stops a program from running, and a log whose timestamps hide an unexplained gap. Fixing what you notice first is not the goal. The deliverable is a bundle of evidence, the minimal repairs, and a handoff note that separates what you proved from what you still suspect.

## The simple version

Think of the bundle as a sealed parcel with a packing slip. The slip (the configuration) claims what is inside and where; the parcel (the filesystem) shows what is actually there; the courier's log (the service log) records when things happened. Diagnosis compares the three and reports every disagreement with evidence. The analogy breaks because a parcel does not run: the program's own permission to execute is a fourth fact the slip never mentions.

## The lab

Run the setup below in your Linux lab. It creates a temporary directory containing `release/` with `bin`, `config`, `data` and `logs`. Nothing outside that directory is touched, and you can delete it afterwards.

```bash
lab=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$lab" || exit 1
mkdir -p release/bin release/config "release/data/quarterly report" release/logs
printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf "service ok\\n"\n' > release/bin/service
chmod 644 release/bin/service
printf 'data_dir=/opt/release/data/quarterly-report\n' > release/config/app.conf
chmod 600 release/config/app.conf
printf 'quarter,revenue\nq3,1200\n' > "release/data/quarterly report/q3.csv"
for i in $(seq 1 20); do printf '2026-09-10T10:%02d:00 INFO tick\n' "$i"; done > release/logs/service.log
printf '2026-09-10T11:45:00 ERROR data_dir missing\n' >> release/logs/service.log
printf 'lab at %s\n' "$lab"
```

## Core mechanics

Work as hypotheses, not fixes. For each suspected problem write the hypothesis, the command that would confirm or refute it, the exact output, and the verdict.

Start with the program: `ls -l release/bin/service` and `release/bin/service` show whether it can execute at all. Then the configuration: `cat release/config/app.conf` names a data directory; `ls -ld release/data/*` shows what exists. Compare the two character by character; a hyphen and a space are different names, and quoting is required to reference the real one. Finally the log: `grep -n ERROR release/logs/service.log` finds the complaint, and a small `awk` pass over the timestamps reveals that the minute-by-minute ticks stop at 10:20 and the next line is 11:45. Ask what could produce an 85-minute silence and note that the log alone cannot prove it.

Select files precisely. Use `find release -type f -newer release/config/app.conf` or `-name` patterns, quote every path with a space, and never run a repair through a glob you have not listed first.

## Runnable experiment

After the setup, run this check without changing anything; it prints one line per fact the diagnosis will rely on. Predict each line first.

```bash
stat -c '%A %n' release/bin/service
# -rw-r--r-- release/bin/service: no execute bit
grep -o 'data_dir=.*' release/config/app.conf; ls -d release/data/*
# quarterly-report versus 'quarterly report': different names
awk -F'[T:]' '{ m=$2*60+$3; if (NR>1 && m-prev>1) print "gap before line", NR ":", m-prev, "minutes"; prev=m }' release/logs/service.log
# gap before line 21: 85 minutes
```

## Minimal repairs and least privilege

`chmod u+x release/bin/service` repairs the execute failure and nothing else. The configuration needs either a corrected `data_dir` value or a renamed directory; choose one, record why, and do not do both. Do not widen permissions on `app.conf`: it is readable by its owner, which is all the service needs. The log gap has no repair; it becomes an open question in the handoff.

## Failure modes

Fixing the visible symptom (the ERROR line) by editing the log proves nothing. Renaming the data directory and editing the config both "work" but leave a future reader unsure which one is canonical. Running `chmod -R 777 release` makes every check pass while destroying the evidence of what was wrong.

## Practical exercise

Deliver a directory containing: `evidence.txt` (each hypothesis with commands and verbatim output), `repairs.sh` (only the commands you actually ran, in order, with a comment per line), and `HANDOFF.md` (three sections: confirmed causes, applied repairs, open questions with the next command you would run). A teammate should be able to re-run the setup and your repairs and reach the same state.

exercise.title: Deliver the diagnosis bundle
exercise.instructions: Run the lab setup, investigate the three suspected problems as hypotheses with evidence, apply the minimal repairs, and produce evidence.txt, repairs.sh and HANDOFF.md so a teammate can reproduce the state from the same setup.
exercise.starter_code:
# evidence.txt skeleton
# H1: the service cannot execute
#   ls -l release/bin/service
#   release/bin/service
# H2: app.conf points at a directory that does not exist
#   cat release/config/app.conf; ls -ld release/data/*
# H3: the log has an unexplained gap before the ERROR
#   awk -F'[T:]' '{ m=$2*60+$3; if (NR>1 && m-prev>1) print "gap before line", NR, m-prev, "minutes"; prev=m }' release/logs/service.log
exercise.deliverable: A handoff directory with evidence.txt, repairs.sh and HANDOFF.md (confirmed causes, applied repairs, open questions).
hints: Quote the data directory path; it contains a space.
Choose one repair for the config/directory mismatch and say why.
The log gap has no repair; record the next investigative command instead.

questions.prompt: `release/bin/service` prints Permission denied and `ls -l` shows `-rw-r--r--`. What is the minimal repair?
questions.explanation: Only the owner's execute bit is missing; add exactly that.
questions.learning_objective: Repair an execution failure with the smallest mode change

questions.prompt: app.conf names `quarterly-report` but the directory is `quarterly report`. What is true?
choices: They are the same path once quoted
They are different names; either the value or the directory must change, and the choice should be recorded
The space is ignored by the kernel
Both must be changed to be safe
questions.correct_answer: They are different names; either the value or the directory must change, and the choice should be recorded
questions.explanation: A hyphen and a space are different characters; pick one canonical repair and document it.
questions.learning_objective: Resolve a path mismatch with one documented repair

questions.prompt: The log ticks every minute until 10:20, then the next line is an ERROR at 11:45. What belongs in the handoff?
choices: A repair that deletes the ERROR line
An open question about the 85-minute silence with the next command to run
A statement that the log proves the service crashed
questions.correct_answer: An open question about the 85-minute silence with the next command to run
questions.explanation: The log shows a gap; it does not prove the cause. Hand it off as an open question.
questions.learning_objective: Distinguish evidence from conclusions in a handoff

questions.prompt: Why must `repairs.sh` contain only the commands you actually ran, in order?
questions.correct_answer: So a teammate can reproduce the exact state from the same setup. Reproducibility is the point of the handoff: same setup, same repairs, same state.
questions.explanation: Reproducibility is the point of the handoff: same setup, same repairs, same state.

questions.prompt: Why does `chmod -R 777 release` make every check pass yet fail the capstone?
questions.correct_answer: It grants read, write and execute to everyone on every file, which is far beyond the confirmed causes, destroys the evidence of what was actually wrong, and leaves the config mismatch and the log gap undiagnosed. The capstone asks for confirmed causes and minimal repairs, not silenced symptoms.
questions.explanation: Symptom silencing is not diagnosis; least privilege and evidence matter.
questions.learning_objective: Explain why blanket permission changes are not a repair
